1	# Scraping edfringe data — API reference
2	
3	Working notes on the edfringe.com data API: where the data lives, how to reach
4	it, the fields it exposes, and the non-obvious bits (pricing, ticket status).
5	Companion to [README.md](README.md), which covers the two scripts
6	(`fetch_shows.py`, `normalize.py`) and the workflows.
7	
8	## The source
9	
10	edfringe.com's "What's On" is a Next.js SPA; the HTML is an empty shell and the
11	shows load client-side from a **GraphQL API** on the Tikketr platform:
12	
13	```
14	POST https://edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com/graphql
15	```
16	
17	Auth is a bearer token from `POST .../token` with the site's **public anonymous
18	credentials** (username `anonymous`, password `2add50c2-ac54-4c1e-b5bc-f8d9ca66a067`).
19	These grant read access to the same public listing everyone sees. Send
20	`Origin: https://www.edfringe.com`.
21	
22	## Reaching it from a Claude Code web session
23	
24	You **can't** hit the API from a web session: the egress proxy blocks
25	`equhost.com` (and edfringe.com itself returns 403 to `WebFetch`). That block is
26	policy — do **not** route around it by creating ad-hoc CI workflows. Anything
27	that touches the live API runs through a sanctioned workflow: the `Scrape
28	edfringe shows (full)` workflow, `Fetch ticket prices (one-off)`, or the
29	`refresh-shows` scheduled task (all on GitHub-hosted runners, under the
30	Claudinite scheduler).
31	
32	This file is the API reference (field lists via GraphQL introspection:
33	`__type` / `__schema`) precisely so that nothing needs to re-fetch it. If it
34	doesn't answer your question, ask the repo owner.
35	
36	## Operations
37	
38	| query | purpose |
39	|---|---|
40	| `events(input: SearchCriteriaInput)` — "EventsSearch" | the paged listing. `per: 50`, `sortBy: TITLE`, a fixed `sortBySeed` for stable paging, `recentlyAdded: ANY \| LAST_SEVEN_DAYS \| LAST_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS`. ~3,900 shows over ~77 pages. Returns a subset of `EventDetail`. |
41	| `event(id: String!, isSlug: Boolean)` | a single show. Pass the slug with `isSlug: true` (the site's URLs are slugs); pass a bare id with `isSlug` false/omitted. Returns the **full** `EventDetail`. Note `id` is **non-null** — a `$id: String` variable is rejected ("not compatible with the type of the current location"); declare `String!`. |
42	| `performancePrices(performanceRef: String)` | **live pricing** for one performance (see below). `performanceRef` = the performance's `boxOfficeId` (e.g. `"1:790001"`). |
43	| `genres` | `GenreOption { label, iconName, value }` — the 10 headline categories. |
44	| `subgenreOptions` | 104 `{ value, label }` subgenre tags. |
45	| `venues` — "VenueTypeAhead" | venue directory (name, address, postcode). |
46	| `priceTypes`, `ageRestrictions`, `accessibilityOptions`, `ticketStatusOptions`, `recentlyAddedOptions` | reference/enum lookups. |
47	| `eventReviews`, `searchEventReviews` | audience reviews per show (`audienceReviewEnabled` gates them). |
48	| auth-only: `login`, `me`, `account`, `basket`, `basketItems`, `tickets`, `transactionFeeInfo`, `offers`, … | booking/account flow; not used. |
49	
50	## `EventDetail` — the per-show fields
51	
52	The `EventsSearch` fragment pulls a subset; `event()` returns all of it.
53	
54	- **Identity/refs:** `id`, `title`, `titleKeyword`, `titleSort`, `slug`, `cmsId`,
55	  `cmsRef`, `boxOfficeId`, `boxOfficeIds`, `boxOfficeIdsKw`, `boxOfficeRef`
56	- **Descriptive:** `description`, `presentedBy`, `countryName`, `purchaseInfo`,
57	  `duration`, `digitalShow`, `audienceReviewEnabled`
58	- **Classification:** `genre` (enum), `subGenre` (String), `subgenres` ([String])
59	- **Suitability:** `ageRestriction` (enum), `accessibility` ([enum]), `accessibilityNotes`
60	- **Dates/availability:** `startingDate`, `endingDate`, `datesDisplay`,
61	  `hasVariousStartingTime`, `onSale`, `onSaleDate`, `canceleld` *(their spelling)*
62	- **Pricing:** `priceType` ([enum] — flags only, **no amounts**), `freeTicketed`
63	- **Location:** `venues`, `spaces`, `geoLocation`, `distance`
64	- **Media/links:** `images`, `socialLinks`
65	- **Nested lists:** `performances`, `attributes`
66	
67	`event()` returns richer nested objects than the search fragment — full venue
68	records (with their own `attributes` bag for accessibility / age / food&drink) and
69	per-space accessibility notes.
70	
71	### Genre & subgenre
72	
73	`genre` is the `Genre` enum: `COMEDY, MUSIC, THEATRE, CHILDRENS_SHOWS, CABARET,
74	CIRCUS, EVENTS, OPERA, SPOKEN_WORD, EXHIBITIONS` (10). `subGenre` is a comma-joined
75	human string whose casing is **inconsistent across shows** ("Alternative Comedy"
76	vs "Alternative comedy"); `subgenres` is the enum-ish list. There are **104**
77	canonical labels (`subgenreOptions`). `normalize.py`'s `unify_subgenre_casing`
78	collapses case-variants to one display casing so the lookup lands on those 104.
79	
80	### `attributes[]` — the per-show key/value bag
81	
82	Keyed by `attributeTypes`: `event_warnings` (content warnings, e.g. "Strong
83	language/swearing, Audience participation"), `age_restrictions` ("16+ (Restriction)"
84	vs "16+ (Guideline)"), `social_media` (facebook/instagram/tiktok/youtube/twitter/website),
85	`babes_in_arms` (policy + age). Venue-level `attributes` also carry `accessibility`
86	and `food_drink`. Content warnings and social links live **here**, not in dedicated
87	fields.
88	
89	### `images[]`
90	
91	Each has `url`, `imageType` (`"Small"` / `"Large"`), `boxOfficeId`, `cmsId`. Images
92	are served from `registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/<uuid>`. `normalize.py`
93	keeps both the Large (`image`) and Small (`smallImage`) variants, selected by
94	`imageType`, and stores just the trailing `<uuid>` — the client re-attaches the
95	host prefix.
96	
97	## Performances
98	
99	`performances[]` (`PerformanceMaster`): `id`, `dateTime`, `estimatedEndDateTime`,
100	`status`, `duration`, `notes`, `cancelled`, `soldOut`, `ticketsAvailable`,
101	**`ticketStatus`**, `boxOfficeId`, `boxOfficeRef`, `accessibility` ([enum]),
102	`badges` ({label, colour}), `concessions`.
103	
104	**`dateTime` is UTC, not Edinburgh wall-clock.** It arrives as
105	`"2026-08-06T11:45:00.000Z"` and the `Z` is real: that show opens its doors at
106	**12:45** during the festival, because August is BST (UTC+1). Slicing the digits
107	straight out of the string — which `normalize.py` did until #time-zone — files
108	every performance an hour early, and the resulting data quietly looks fine: the
109	"7am Oboe Rave" sat at 06:00, "Jokes At Noon" at 11:00, and Shakespeare for
110	Breakfast (a 10am institution) at 09:00. Those shows-named-after-their-own-time
111	are the cheapest way to check a fresh scrape landed on the right hour. The
112	conversion lives in `normalize.local_date_start` and happens exactly once, at
113	the edge; everything the pipeline writes downstream is Edinburgh wall-clock.
114	
115	**`ticketStatus` is the signal for "can I get a ticket".** Values seen in a full
116	scrape: `TICKETS_AVAILABLE`, `TWO_FOR_ONE`, `FREE_NON_TICKETED`, `FREE_TICKETED`,
117	`PREVIEW_SHOW`, `EVENT_SPECIFIC`, `NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` (and `SOLD_OUT`
118	appears once tickets actually sell out; the authoritative set is
119	`ticketStatusOptions`). The site treats `SOLD_OUT` and
120	`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` as "no ticket available" (→ SOLD OUT stamp) and
121	everything else as available. **Do not rely on the `soldOut` boolean** — a
122	performance can be `soldOut: false` yet `ticketStatus: NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`
123	(nothing to sell online). e.g. Daniel Sloss 14 Aug: `soldOut:false`,
124	`ticketStatus:NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`.
125	
126	## Pricing (the non-obvious part)
127	
128	`event()` and the search results carry **no price amounts** — `priceType` is just
129	flags (`priceTypes`: `TWO_FOR_ONE, FREE, FRIENDS_TWO_FOR_ONE, GROUP_DISCOUNTS,
130	PAY_WHAT_YOU_WANT, PREVIEW`). Real money comes only from **`performancePrices`**,
131	per performance:
132	
133	```
134	performancePrices(performanceRef: "1:790001")
135	  -> ResponseWrapperOfPerformancePriceDto { success, error, message, result }
136	     result: PerformancePriceDto {
137	       performanceId, isFromAllocation, allocationDetails,
138	       performancePercentageRemaining, performanceAvailabilityLevel,
139	       prices: [ Price ]
140	     }
141	```
142	
143	`Price` (one per band): `priceBandId`, `pricetype` ("Price A"/"Price B"/…),
144	`priceValue`, `totalPrice`, `transactionFeesPrice`, `outsideFeesPrice`,
145	`feeInTicketPrice`, `description`, `priceBandReservationLevel` ("SEAT"), `seats`
146	(bool), **`seatPercentageRemaining`** (live), `availabilityLevel`, `hideFullPrice`,
147	`fees` ([{code, title, value, feeType:"HANDLING"}]), `concessions`
148	([{code, title, concPrice, feeExempt, …}]), `eventFeeExempt`, `handlingFeeExempt`.
149	
150	Key facts:
151	- **There is no bulk price endpoint** — amounts are one call **per performance**.
152	- Price bands are typically **identical across a show's performances**, so ~one
153	  call per *show* gives representative pricing (still ~3,900 calls for the whole
154	  festival).
155	- `performancePrices` returns **live** availability (`seatPercentageRemaining`,
156	  `performancePercentageRemaining`) — real-time, not something to bake into the
157	  nightly static scrape.
158	
159	### What the response actually looks like
160	
161	Captured from `performancePrices("1:790001")` — Daniel Sloss: BITTER, 14 Aug.
162	Four things the field
163	list above doesn't tell you, each of which the extraction has to handle:
164	
165	- **Amounts are JSON *strings***, not numbers: `"priceValue": "29.50"`. Parse,
166	  don't assume.
167	- **`totalPrice` equals `priceValue`.** The booking fee is broken out in
168	  `transactionFeesPrice` (`"1.50"`) with `feeInTicketPrice: false` — so the band
169	  value *is* the advertised face price and the fee is added at checkout. Don't
170	  read `totalPrice` as "price with fees".
171	- **`concessions` is dominated by a £0.00 "Personal Assistant" band** (code
172	  `PA`) — the companion ticket for a disabled patron's carer, present on
173	  essentially every show. Taking the literal cheapest concession records a
174	  £29.50 show as costing nothing; only concessions **above £0** are prices.
175	- **A sold-out performance still returns prices.** The 14 Aug performance is
176	  `performancePercentageRemaining: 0` /
177	  `ticketStatus: NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` and prices come back regardless,
178	  so the price pass needn't pick an available performance.
179	
180	The three bands ("Price A/B/C" at £29.50 / £25.00 / £22.50) were **identical
181	across both of that show's performances**, which is the assumption
182	`fetch_prices.py --sample-performances N` re-checks: it prices N performances of
183	a show and reports whether the bands agree.
184	
185	## How the repo turns this into the site
186	
187	`fetch_shows.py` → raw pages (git-ignored cache). `normalize.py` →
188	`data/normalized/shows.json` (master), `data/venues.json` (the shared lookup:
189	`{venues, rooms, genres, subgenres}`), and compact `data/days/2026-08-DD.json`
190	(genre/room/subgenres referenced by index into the lookup, flags as 1/0). See
191	[README.md](README.md) for the exact layout and the daily/full workflows.
192

`__type` / `__schema`) precisely so that nothing needs to re-fetch it. If it
doesn't answer your question, ask the repo owner.

## Operations

| query | purpose |
|---|---|
| `events(input: SearchCriteriaInput)` — "EventsSearch" | the paged listing. `per: 50`, `sortBy: TITLE`, a fixed `sortBySeed` for stable paging, `recentlyAdded: ANY \| LAST_SEVEN_DAYS \| LAST_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS`. ~3,900 shows over ~77 pages. Returns a subset of `EventDetail`. |
| `event(id: String!, isSlug: Boolean)` | a single show. Pass the slug with `isSlug: true` (the site's URLs are slugs); pass a bare id with `isSlug` false/omitted. Returns the **full** `EventDetail`. Note `id` is **non-null** — a `$id: String` variable is rejected ("not compatible with the type of the current location"); declare `String!`. |
| `performancePrices(performanceRef: String)` | **live pricing** for one performance (see below). `performanceRef` = the performance's `boxOfficeId` (e.g. `"1:790001"`). |
| `genres` | `GenreOption { label, iconName, value }` — the 10 headline categories. |
| `subgenreOptions` | 104 `{ value, label }` subgenre tags. |
| `venues` — "VenueTypeAhead" | venue directory (name, address, postcode). |
| `priceTypes`, `ageRestrictions`, `accessibilityOptions`, `ticketStatusOptions`, `recentlyAddedOptions` | reference/enum lookups. |
| `eventReviews`, `searchEventReviews` | audience reviews per show (`audienceReviewEnabled` gates them). |
| auth-only: `login`, `me`, `account`, `basket`, `basketItems`, `tickets`, `transactionFeeInfo`, `offers`, … | booking/account flow; not used. |

## `EventDetail` — the per-show fields

The `EventsSearch` fragment pulls a subset; `event()` returns all of it.

- **Identity/refs:** `id`, `title`, `titleKeyword`, `titleSort`, `slug`, `cmsId`,
  `cmsRef`, `boxOfficeId`, `boxOfficeIds`, `boxOfficeIdsKw`, `boxOfficeRef`
- **Descriptive:** `description`, `presentedBy`, `countryName`, `purchaseInfo`,
  `duration`, `digitalShow`, `audienceReviewEnabled`
- **Classification:** `genre` (enum), `subGenre` (String), `subgenres` ([String])
- **Suitability:** `ageRestriction` (enum), `accessibility` ([enum]), `accessibilityNotes`
- **Dates/availability:** `startingDate`, `endingDate`, `datesDisplay`,
  `hasVariousStartingTime`, `onSale`, `onSaleDate`, `canceleld` *(their spelling)*
- **Pricing:** `priceType` ([enum] — flags only, **no amounts**), `freeTicketed`
- **Location:** `venues`, `spaces`, `geoLocation`, `distance`
- **Media/links:** `images`, `socialLinks`
- **Nested lists:** `performances`, `attributes`

`event()` returns richer nested objects than the search fragment — full venue
records (with their own `attributes` bag for accessibility / age / food&drink) and
per-space accessibility notes.

### Genre & subgenre

`genre` is the `Genre` enum: `COMEDY, MUSIC, THEATRE, CHILDRENS_SHOWS, CABARET,
CIRCUS, EVENTS, OPERA, SPOKEN_WORD, EXHIBITIONS` (10). `subGenre` is a comma-joined
human string whose casing is **inconsistent across shows** ("Alternative Comedy"
vs "Alternative comedy"); `subgenres` is the enum-ish list. There are **104**
canonical labels (`subgenreOptions`). `normalize.py`'s `unify_subgenre_casing`
collapses case-variants to one display casing so the lookup lands on those 104.

### `attributes[]` — the per-show key/value bag

Keyed by `attributeTypes`: `event_warnings` (content warnings, e.g. "Strong
language/swearing, Audience participation"), `age_restrictions` ("16+ (Restriction)"
vs "16+ (Guideline)"), `social_media` (facebook/instagram/tiktok/youtube/twitter/website),
`babes_in_arms` (policy + age). Venue-level `attributes` also carry `accessibility`
and `food_drink`. Content warnings and social links live **here**, not in dedicated
fields.

### `images[]`

Each has `url`, `imageType` (`"Small"` / `"Large"`), `boxOfficeId`, `cmsId`. Images
are served from `registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/<uuid>`. `normalize.py`
keeps both the Large (`image`) and Small (`smallImage`) variants, selected by
`imageType`, and stores just the trailing `<uuid>` — the client re-attaches the
host prefix.

## Performances

`performances[]` (`PerformanceMaster`): `id`, `dateTime`, `estimatedEndDateTime`,
`status`, `duration`, `notes`, `cancelled`, `soldOut`, `ticketsAvailable`,
**`ticketStatus`**, `boxOfficeId`, `boxOfficeRef`, `accessibility` ([enum]),
`badges` ({label, colour}), `concessions`.

**`dateTime` is UTC, not Edinburgh wall-clock.** It arrives as
`"2026-08-06T11:45:00.000Z"` and the `Z` is real: that show opens its doors at
**12:45** during the festival, because August is BST (UTC+1). Slicing the digits
straight out of the string — which `normalize.py` did until #time-zone — files
every performance an hour early, and the resulting data quietly looks fine: the
"7am Oboe Rave" sat at 06:00, "Jokes At Noon" at 11:00, and Shakespeare for
Breakfast (a 10am institution) at 09:00. Those shows-named-after-their-own-time
are the cheapest way to check a fresh scrape landed on the right hour. The
conversion lives in `normalize.local_date_start` and happens exactly once, at
the edge; everything the pipeline writes downstream is Edinburgh wall-clock.

**`ticketStatus` is the signal for "can I get a ticket".** Values seen in a full
scrape: `TICKETS_AVAILABLE`, `TWO_FOR_ONE`, `FREE_NON_TICKETED`, `FREE_TICKETED`,
`PREVIEW_SHOW`, `EVENT_SPECIFIC`, `NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` (and `SOLD_OUT`
appears once tickets actually sell out; the authoritative set is
`ticketStatusOptions`). The site treats `SOLD_OUT` and
`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` as "no ticket available" (→ SOLD OUT stamp) and
everything else as available. **Do not rely on the `soldOut` boolean** — a
performance can be `soldOut: false` yet `ticketStatus: NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`
(nothing to sell online). e.g. Daniel Sloss 14 Aug: `soldOut:false`,
`ticketStatus:NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`.

## Pricing (the non-obvious part)

`event()` and the search results carry **no price amounts** — `priceType` is just
flags (`priceTypes`: `TWO_FOR_ONE, FREE, FRIENDS_TWO_FOR_ONE, GROUP_DISCOUNTS,
PAY_WHAT_YOU_WANT, PREVIEW`). Real money comes only from **`performancePrices`**,
per performance:

```
performancePrices(performanceRef: "1:790001")
  -> ResponseWrapperOfPerformancePriceDto { success, error, message, result }
     result: PerformancePriceDto {
       performanceId, isFromAllocation, allocationDetails,
       performancePercentageRemaining, performanceAvailabilityLevel,
       prices: [ Price ]
     }
```

`Price` (one per band): `priceBandId`, `pricetype` ("Price A"/"Price B"/…),
`priceValue`, `totalPrice`, `transactionFeesPrice`, `outsideFeesPrice`,
`feeInTicketPrice`, `description`, `priceBandReservationLevel` ("SEAT"), `seats`
(bool), **`seatPercentageRemaining`** (live), `availabilityLevel`, `hideFullPrice`,
`fees` ([{code, title, value, feeType:"HANDLING"}]), `concessions`
([{code, title, concPrice, feeExempt, …}]), `eventFeeExempt`, `handlingFeeExempt`.

Key facts:
- **There is no bulk price endpoint** — amounts are one call **per performance**.
- Price bands are typically **identical across a show's performances**, so ~one
  call per *show* gives representative pricing (still ~3,900 calls for the whole
  festival).
- `performancePrices` returns **live** availability (`seatPercentageRemaining`,
  `performancePercentageRemaining`) — real-time, not something to bake into the
  nightly static scrape.

### What the response actually looks like

Captured from `performancePrices("1:790001")` — Daniel Sloss: BITTER, 14 Aug.
Four things the field
list above doesn't tell you, each of which the extraction has to handle:

- **Amounts are JSON *strings***, not numbers: `"priceValue": "29.50"`. Parse,
  don't assume.
- **`totalPrice` equals `priceValue`.** The booking fee is broken out in
  `transactionFeesPrice` (`"1.50"`) with `feeInTicketPrice: false` — so the band
  value *is* the advertised face price and the fee is added at checkout. Don't
  read `totalPrice` as "price with fees".
- **`concessions` is dominated by a £0.00 "Personal Assistant" band** (code
  `PA`) — the companion ticket for a disabled patron's carer, present on
  essentially every show. Taking the literal cheapest concession records a
  £29.50 show as costing nothing; only concessions **above £0** are prices.
- **A sold-out performance still returns prices.** The 14 Aug performance is
  `performancePercentageRemaining: 0` /
  `ticketStatus: NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` and prices come back regardless,
  so the price pass needn't pick an available performance.

The three bands ("Price A/B/C" at £29.50 / £25.00 / £22.50) were **identical
across both of that show's performances**, which is the assumption
`fetch_prices.py --sample-performances N` re-checks: it prices N performances of
a show and reports whether the bands agree.

## How the repo turns this into the site

`fetch_shows.py` → raw pages (git-ignored cache). `normalize.py` →
`data/normalized/shows.json` (master), `data/venues.json` (the shared lookup:
`{venues, rooms, genres, subgenres}`), and compact `data/days/2026-08-DD.json`
(genre/room/subgenres referenced by index into the lookup, flags as 1/0). See
[README.md](README.md) for the exact layout and the daily/full workflows.

lastPrompt: For the daily files - you can have the correct prices per day of performance. Why have a specifc rule about previews and cutoffs? This could be solved better.

content.text:
You're right, and I'd drop the preview/cutoff idea. It was a patch that keeps the current "one price per show" model and tries to guess which single performance is *representative* — which just trades one wrong guess for another (it would still collapse the £15 weekday / £16 weekend split, and it bakes festival semantics into the scraper). The data model you already have supports the honest answer.

## The better design: price is a property of the performance, not the show

The site is already sharded by day — each `data/days/2026-08-DD.json` record describes *that day's performance* of a show (`start`, `soldOut`, `ts`, and today a copied show-level `pm`). The API is also per-performance: `performancePrices` takes a `performanceRef`, one call per performance, and SCRAPING.md confirms sold-out/past performances still answer. So the pieces line up:

1. **Cache** (`data/prices.json`): store bands *per date* per show instead of one record — e.g. `{"dates": {"2026-08-05": {...bands}, "2026-08-08": {...}}}`, or band-sets with the dates they cover.
2. **Day files**: `normalize.py` folds each date's own price into that day's record. The Aug 5 file honestly says £8.50 (that *was* the preview price), Aug 8 says £15, a Saturday says £16. No rule ever mentions "preview" — a price difference for any reason (previews, weekend uplift, final-week discount) falls out of the same mechanism.
3. **Catalogue** (`shows.json` `priceMin`/`priceMax`): becomes the true min–max across the run, and the planner — which is already day-scoped — can show the exact price for the day being planned.

## The one real constraint: call budget

There's no bulk endpoint, so full fidelity is ~3,664 paid shows × ~20+ performances ≈ **75k+ calls** — at the scraper's polite 1–2.5s spacing that's ~40 hours, versus ~2 hours for the current pass (and GitHub-hosted runner jobs cap at 6 hours). The practical shape is adaptive sampling, which is still rule-free:

- Price a small stratified sample per show — first, last, mid-run, one weekend day (~4 calls). The band-fingerprint machinery for comparing them already exists (`band_fingerprint`, `--sample-performances`).
- **If all samples agree** (probably ~70% of shows, given 28% were preview-priced): one band set covers every date. ~4 calls, done.
- **If they differ**: enumerate that show's remaining performances. Only the varying minority pays the full per-performance cost.

Rough total ≈ 35–40k calls — chunkable across runs with the existing `--limit`/resume support, and unlike today it converges on data that's *correct by construction* rather than representative by assumption. The nightly `refresh-shows` path wouldn't need to change: prices stay a hand-triggered pass, just a smarter one.

The one heuristic I'd keep is not about previews: skip *past* dates on re-runs — not because their prices are wrong, but because they're unbuyable and not worth a call.

> ⚠️ Open: this is a design assessment only — nothing implemented. If you want it, the work is (1) restructure `fetch_prices.py` to per-date records with adaptive sampling, (2) teach `normalize.py` to fold per-day prices into day files and run-wide min/max into `shows.json`, (3) trigger the sanctioned price workflow to rebuild the cache (the scrape itself can't run from this sandbox — the proxy blocks the API host).

content.text:
You were right that I gave up too easily, though the mechanism is slightly different from what you guessed. Here's what I found.

## How I checked

The API host (`equhost.com`) is blocked by this session's egress policy — a hard 403 at the proxy, which I'm not allowed to route around. But `www.edfringe.com` itself is reachable, so I pulled the site's own JavaScript bundles (1.3MB across 24 chunks) and recovered the **complete set of GraphQL operations the client is built against** — 60+ queries and mutations, with their full field selections.

## There is no bulk price *field* — but there is a bulk *request*

Three things are now settled from the client's own query text, not inference:

- `performancePrices(performanceRef: $performanceId)` takes **exactly one** ref. There's no list variant, no `performanceRefs`, no event-level price query.
- There *is* a genuine bulk query I hadn't documented — `GetPerformances` → `performances(input: SearchCriteriaInput!)`, paged and searchable — but its `PerformanceDetail` fragment has **no price fields at all** (id, title, dateTime, status, ticketStatus, boxOfficeId, venue, space, event, concessions… and that's it).
- `EventDetail` carries only `priceType` flags, as documented.

So money genuinely only comes from `performancePrices`, one ref at a time. **But that's a field-level constraint, not a network-level one.** GraphQL lets you alias the same field many times in a single document, so one HTTP request can carry every performance of a show:

```graphql
query BulkPrices {
  p0: performancePrices(performanceRef: "61:185473") { ...B }
  p1: performancePrices(performanceRef: "61:185471") { ...B }
  ...
}
```

481	                data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
482	        except (URLError, HTTPError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
483	            print(f"  WARNING: geocoding failed for a chunk: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
484	            continue
485	        for item in data.get("result", []):
486	            res = item.get("result")
487	            if res and res.get("latitude") is not None:
488	                coords[item["query"]] = (round(res["latitude"], 6),
489	                                         round(res["longitude"], 6))
490	    return coords

493	def unify_subgenre_casing(master: list[dict]) -> None:
494	    """Collapse case-variant subgenres to one display casing, in place.
495	
496	    The festival's free-text `subGenre` is inconsistently cased across shows, so
497	    the same tag arrives as both "Alternative Comedy" and "Alternative comedy" —
498	    which would otherwise show as two distinct tags. For each case-folded
499	    subgenre, pick the most title-cased variant (the festival's own labels are
500	    Title Case; the lowercase forms are data-entry slips, even when commoner),
501	    breaking ties by frequency then alphabetically. Deterministic across runs,
502	    and it keeps the nicer form ("LGBTQ+", "Sci-Fi", "Artist(s) of Colour").
503	    """
504	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
505	    variants: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
506	    for show in master:
507	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
508	            counts[label] = counts.get(label, 0) + 1
509	            variants.setdefault(label.casefold(), set()).add(label)
510	
511	    def rank(v: str) -> tuple:
512	        titleish = sum(1 for w in v.split() if w[:1].isupper())
513	        return (-titleish, -counts[v], v)
514	
515	    canon = {key: sorted(vs, key=rank)[0] for key, vs in variants.items()}
516	    for show in master:
517	        seen: set[str] = set()
518	        out: list[str] = []
519	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
520	            picked = canon.get(label.casefold(), label)
521	            if picked.casefold() not in seen:
522	                seen.add(picked.casefold())
523	                out.append(picked)
524	        show["subgenres"] = out
525

527	def extend_lookup(prior: list[str] | None, values: set[str]) -> list[str]:
528	    """One lookup list, extended APPEND-ONLY: every entry the previous
529	    venues.json published keeps its index forever, and anything new is appended
530	    (sorted, so a rebuild is deterministic).
531	
532	    This is a correctness constraint, not tidiness. A browser holds these files
533	    on independent clocks — shows.min.json for four days, venues.json for one
534	    (shared/data-cache.js) — so a four-day-old catalogue is routinely decoded
535	    against a venues.json fetched today. Re-sorting the whole list from scratch
536	    would silently shift every index under that stale catalogue and relabel
537	    shows' genres and rooms. Appending cannot: an index minted at any point
538	    stays valid for every version that follows.
539	
540	    The corollary is that an entry is never dropped once published, even when
541	    the current master no longer uses it. These are a few hundred short strings;
542	    a stale-free decode is worth more than the bytes.
543	    """
544	    out = list(prior or [])
545	    known = set(out)
546	    out.extend(sorted(v for v in values if v not in known))
547	    return out
548

550	def build_lookups(master: list[dict],
551	                  prior: dict | None = None
552	                  ) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
553	    """The global (genres, rooms, subgenres, ticketStatuses, ageRestrictions)
554	    lookup lists: every distinct genre, room, subgenre, per-performance ticket
555	    status and age restriction across all shows. A show references them by index
556	    in the day files and in shows.min.json; the lists ship once, alongside the
557	    venues (run()).
558	
559	    `prior` is the previously published venues.json, whose ordering is preserved
560	    verbatim — see extend_lookup for why the lists are append-only.
561	    """
562	    prior = prior or {}
563	    genres = extend_lookup(prior.get("genres"), {s["genre"] for s in master if s.get("genre")})
564	    rooms = extend_lookup(prior.get("rooms"), {s["room"] for s in master if s.get("room")})
565	    subgenres = extend_lookup(prior.get("subgenres"),
566	                              {sg for s in master for sg in s.get("subgenres") or []})
567	    ticket_statuses = extend_lookup(prior.get("ticketStatuses"),
568	                                    {p.get("status") for s in master
569	                                     for p in s.get("performances") or [] if p.get("status")})
570	    age_restrictions = extend_lookup(prior.get("ageRestrictions"),
571	                                     {s["ageRestriction"] for s in master if s.get("ageRestriction")})
572	    return genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses, age_restrictions

575	def fringe_day(date: str, start: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
576	    """Which fringe day a performance belongs to, and its start within that day.
577	
578	    A performance before FRINGE_DAY_START is part of the night before: its date
579	    moves back one and its start time moves forward past 24:00, so 00:30 on the
580	    15th is the 14th at "24:30". Everything from 06:00 on is left exactly as it
581	    is — including the 06:00 breakfast shows, which belong to the morning they
582	    happen in and not to the night that just ended.
583	
584	    >>> fringe_day("2026-08-15", "00:30")
585	    ('2026-08-14', '24:30')
586	    >>> fringe_day("2026-08-15", "06:00")
587	    ('2026-08-15', '06:00')
588	    """
589	    hh, mm = int(start[:2]), int(start[3:5])
590	    minutes = hh * 60 + mm
591	    if minutes >= FRINGE_DAY_START_MIN:
592	        return date, start
593	    prev = (datetime.strptime(date, "%Y-%m-%d") - timedelta(days=1)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
594	    return prev, f"{hh + 24:02d}:{mm:02d}"
595

597	def build_day_files(master: list[dict], genre_ix: dict[str, int],
598	                    room_ix: dict[str, int], sub_ix: dict[str, int],
599	                    ts_ix: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, list]:
600	    """Bucket shows by fringe day (06:00 → 06:00, see FRINGE_DAY_START) into
601	    minimal per-day records. A performance after midnight lands in the previous
602	    day's file with an extended `start` ("24:30" for 00:30) — see fringe_day.
603	
604	    Each record is kept small:
605	
606	      * `genre` / `room` — pointers into the global `genres` / `rooms` lookup
607	        lists (shipped once with the venues), not the strings themselves.
608	        `room` is -1 when the show has no specific room.
609	      * `subs` — the show's subgenres as pointers into the global `subgenres`
610	        lookup list; an empty list when the festival tagged none (~2%).
611	      * `ts` — this performance's ticket status as a pointer into the global
612	        `ticketStatuses` lookup (-1 if unknown). This is the reliable "can I get
613	        a ticket" signal; the `soldOut` flag is not (a show can be soldOut:false
614	        yet have no online allocation).
615	      * `free` / `soldOut` — 1/0 rather than true/false.
616	      * `blurb` — omitted. It is kept in the master (the scraped data) but the
617	        site never renders it, so it is left out of the per-day payload.
618	    """
619	    days: dict[str, list] = {}
620	    seen: set[tuple] = set()   # (id, day, start) — drop duplicate performances
621	    for show in master:
622	        for p in show.get("performances", []):
623	            # Bucket by the fringe day, not the calendar one: a 1 September
624	            # 00:30 show is the last night of the run, and a 1 August 00:30 show
625	            # belongs to a July night the festival never had, so it drops out.
626	            date, start = fringe_day(p["date"], p["start"])
627	            if not date.startswith(AUGUST_PREFIX):
628	                continue
629	            key = (show["id"], date, start)
630	            if key in seen:
631	                continue
632	            seen.add(key)
633	            rec = {
634	                "id": show["id"],
635	                "title": show["title"],
636	                "genre": genre_ix.get(show.get("genre"), -1),
637	                "subs": [sub_ix[sg] for sg in show.get("subgenres") or []
638	                         if sg in sub_ix],
639	                "venue": show["venue"],
640	                "room": room_ix.get(show.get("room"), -1),
641	                "start": start,
642	                "duration": show["duration"],
643	                "free": 1 if show["free"] else 0,
644	                "soldOut": 1 if p["soldOut"] else 0,
645	                "ts": ts_ix.get(p.get("status"), -1),
646	                "slug": show["slug"],
647	            }
648	            # Cheapest band only: the Now page's price filter asks "what can I
649	            # see for up to £X", which the lowest band answers. The full range
650	            # lives in the planner's catalogue, which isn't size-constrained the
651	            # way a day file is. Omitted when the price is unknown.
652	            if show.get("priceMin") is not None:
653	                rec["pm"] = show["priceMin"]
654	            days.setdefault(date, []).append(rec)
655	    for date in days:
656	        days[date].sort(key=lambda x: (x["start"], x["title"] or ""))
657	    return days

661	# Compact wire form of the master (data/normalized/shows.min.json).
662	#
663	# The planner downloads this, not the 7 MB master. It is packed against the same
664	# venues.json lookups the day files use, so it carries no dictionaries of its own,
665	# and the packing is lossless — plan/plan.js rebuilds the full records from it.

668	def month_day_key(date: str) -> int:
669	    """A 2026 date as an MMDD integer: "2026-08-07" -> 807, "2026-07-24" -> 724.
670	
671	    Every performance is in 2026 (the festival year), so the year is implied and
672	    only the month/day need storing; the client re-attaches "2026-".
673	    """
674	    return int(date[5:7] + date[8:10])

677	def venue_name_rebuildable(show: dict, venues: dict) -> bool:
678	    """True when a show's venueName is exactly "<room> at <venue name>" (or the
679	    bare venue name when it has no room), so it can be dropped from the wire form
680	    and rebuilt client-side from the venue code + room. False for the handful of
681	    shows with no resolvable venue (or any venueName that wouldn't rebuild
682	    byte-for-byte) — those keep their venueName verbatim, so packing stays
683	    lossless whatever the data does."""
684	    code = show.get("venue")
685	    if not code or code not in venues:
686	        return False
687	    name = venues[code].get("name")
688	    room = show.get("room")
689	    rebuilt = f"{room} at {name}" if room else name
690	    return rebuilt == show.get("venueName")

693	def minify_master(master: list[dict], genre_ix: dict[str, int], room_ix: dict[str, int],
694	                  sub_ix: dict[str, int], age_ix: dict[str, int],
695	                  venues: dict) -> list[dict]:
696	    """Pack the full master into the compact records the planner downloads.
697	
698	    Each field is either shortened, indexed into a shared venues.json lookup, or
699	    dropped when it can be reconstructed:
700	
701	      * `g`/`rm`/`ar` — genre, room and age restriction as indices into the
702	        global genres/rooms/ageRestrictions lists (-1 when absent).
703	      * `sg` — subgenres as indices into the global subgenres list.
704	      * `vn` — venueName, kept ONLY when it can't be rebuilt from `v` + `rm`
705	        (venue_name_rebuildable); present-but-null for the no-venue shows.
706	      * `si` — smallImage, kept ONLY when it differs from `im` (image); otherwise
707	        the client mirrors image.
708	      * `f` — free as 1/0.
709	      * `p[].d` — the performance date as an MMDD int.
710	      * `im` — the bare image GUID; the client re-attaches the host prefix.
711	
712	    Each performance keeps only its identity — the date and start time that name
713	    it. Its ticket status and soldOut flag are the two fields that change through
714	    the day, and they live in the availability sidecar (build_availability) so
715	    this file can be cached for days without freezing them. rehydrateShows in
716	    plan/lib/hydrate.js puts the two halves back together.
717	    """
718	    out: list[dict] = []
719	    for s in master:
720	        rec: dict = {
721	            "i": s["id"],
722	            "t": s["title"],
723	            "sl": s["slug"],
724	            "g": genre_ix.get(s.get("genre"), -1),
725	            "sg": [sub_ix[sg] for sg in s.get("subgenres") or [] if sg in sub_ix],
726	            "c": s.get("company"),
727	            "d": s.get("duration"),
728	            "ar": age_ix.get(s.get("ageRestriction"), -1),
729	            "f": 1 if s.get("free") else 0,
730	            "im": s.get("image"),
731	        }
732	        # Real ticket prices, in pounds. Omitted entirely when unknown, which
733	        # the client must not confuse with free (`f`) — see apply_prices.
734	        if s.get("priceMin") is not None:
735	            rec["pm"] = s["priceMin"]
736	            if s.get("priceMax") not in (None, s["priceMin"]):
737	                rec["px"] = s["priceMax"]
738	        if s.get("smallImage") != s.get("image"):
739	            rec["si"] = s.get("smallImage")
740	        rec["b"] = s.get("blurb") or ""
741	        rec["v"] = s.get("venue")
742	        if not venue_name_rebuildable(s, venues):
743	            rec["vn"] = s.get("venueName")
744	        rec["rm"] = room_ix.get(s.get("room"), -1)
745	        rec["p"] = [{
746	            "d": month_day_key(p["date"]),
747	            "s": p["start"],
748	        } for p in s.get("performances") or []]
749	        out.append(rec)
750	    return out

753	def performance_keys(performances: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
754	    """Name each of a show's performances: ["807|21:15", "807|21:15#1", ...].
755	
756	    Deliberately content-addressed rather than positional. The sidecar and the
757	    catalogue are cached on different clocks, so the client may hold a
758	    four-day-old catalogue beside availability fetched an hour ago; a bare index
759	    into the performance array would silently misalign the moment a show gained
760	    or lost a date. A date plus a start time names the same performance in both
761	    files or matches nothing at all.
762	
763	    A handful of shows (4 of 4114) list the same date and start twice, with
764	    genuinely different ticket statuses — a preview and a regular sitting, say.
765	    Those are not the same performance and must not collapse into one, so the
766	    second and later occurrences carry a "#n" suffix. It is positional, and so
767	    carries the misalignment risk the rest of this scheme avoids; it is confined
768	    to the duplicates, where there is nothing else to tell them apart.
769	
770	    plan/lib/hydrate.js walks the same array in the same order — keep the two in
771	    step.
772	    """
773	    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
774	    keys: list[str] = []
775	    for p in performances:
776	        base = f"{month_day_key(p['date'])}|{p['start']}"
777	        n = seen.get(base, 0)
778	        seen[base] = n + 1
779	        keys.append(base if n == 0 else f"{base}#{n}")
780	    return keys
781

783	def build_availability(master: list[dict]) -> dict:
784	    """The availability sidecar: {"v", "ts", "a", "o"}.
785	
786	      * `ts` — this file's OWN ticket-status list. Unlike the day files and the
787	        catalogue, the sidecar indexes into nothing external: it is rewritten
788	        hourly and must not depend on venues.json having been refetched in the
789	        same breath.
790	      * `a`  — {show id: {performance key: index into `ts`}}. Performances with
791	        no status at all are omitted rather than mapped to -1; the client reads a
792	        missing entry as "unknown", which is what it is.
793	      * `o`  — {show id: [performance key, ...]} for sold-out performances only.
794	        A separate map because the flag is almost always false (the festival
795	        reports a lost allocation as a *status*, not as soldOut — see
796	        SCRAPING.md), so a per-performance boolean would cost far more than the
797	        handful of keys it carries.
798	
799	    Everything here is derived from the master, which stays the single source of
800	    truth: the sidecar is a projection of it, never an input.
801	    """
802	    statuses = sorted({p.get("status") for s in master
803	                       for p in s.get("performances") or [] if p.get("status")})
804	    ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(statuses)}
805	    avail: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
806	    sold: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
807	    for show in master:
808	        performances = show.get("performances") or []
809	        by_key: dict[str, int] = {}
810	        sold_keys: list[str] = []
811	        for key, p in zip(performance_keys(performances), performances):
812	            status = p.get("status")
813	            if status:
814	                by_key[key] = ix[status]
815	            if p.get("soldOut"):
816	                sold_keys.append(key)
817	        if by_key:
818	            avail[show["id"]] = by_key
819	        if sold_keys:
820	            sold[show["id"]] = sold_keys
821	    return {"v": 1, "ts": statuses, "a": avail, "o": sold}
822

824	def build_descriptions(master: list[dict]) -> dict:
825	    """The descriptions sidecar: {"v": 1, "d": {slug: text}}.
826	
827	    Falls back to a show's `blurb` when it has no `description` — masters
828	    scraped before descriptions were retained carry only the truncated blurb,
829	    and half a sentence is still better for search than nothing. Shows with
830	    neither are omitted entirely rather than mapped to "", which keeps the file
831	    to what it is actually for.
832	
833	    Not packed against venues.json like the other wire files: it is keyed by
834	    slug and indexes into nothing, so it can be regenerated, cached and expired
835	    on its own schedule without touching the lookup lists.
836	    """
837	    out: dict[str, str] = {}
838	    for show in master:
839	        slug = show.get("slug")
840	        text = show.get("description") or show.get("blurb") or ""
841	        if slug and text:
842	            out[slug] = text
843	    return {"v": 1, "d": out}

883	def write_derived_outputs(master: list[dict], venues: dict, venues_path: Path,
884	                          days_dir: Path, master_min_path: Path,
885	                          descriptions_path: Path, prices_path: Path,
886	                          availability_path: Path) -> int:
887	    """Write everything derived from the master + venue map: the shared lookup
888	    file (venues.json), the per-day now-page files, the compact planner file
889	    (shows.min.json) and its availability + descriptions sidecars. Returns the
890	    number of day files written.
891	
892	    The lookup lists are built once here and indexed into by both the day files
893	    and shows.min.json, so the two stay in lockstep with a single source of truth.
894	
895	    Every output is a pure function of the master, the venue map and the price
896	    cache, so re-running it over an unchanged master rewrites every file
897	    byte-for-byte identically. The hourly ticket refresh leans on exactly that:
898	    it touches the master's statuses and calls this, and only the files that
899	    actually carry a status come back changed.
900	    """
901	    # Real ticket amounts, folded in before anything is packed so the master and
902	    # both wire forms agree on what a show costs.
903	    known = apply_prices(master, load_prices(prices_path))
904	    print(f"  priced {known}/{len(master)} shows from {prices_path.name}")
905	
906	    # The lookup lists extend the ones already published rather than being
907	    # re-derived from scratch — see extend_lookup: clients decode a cached
908	    # catalogue against a newer venues.json, so indices must never move.
909	    prior_lookups = json.loads(venues_path.read_text()) if venues_path.exists() else {}
910	    genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses, age_restrictions = build_lookups(
911	        master, prior_lookups)
912	    write_json(venues_path, {"venues": venues, "rooms": rooms, "genres": genres,
913	                             "subgenres": subgenres, "ticketStatuses": ticket_statuses,
914	                             "ageRestrictions": age_restrictions})
915	
916	    genre_ix = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genres)}
917	    room_ix = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(rooms)}
918	    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subgenres)}
919	    ts_ix = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(ticket_statuses)}
920	    age_ix = {a: i for i, a in enumerate(age_restrictions)}
921	
922	    # Compact planner payload (packed against the lookups just written), and the
923	    # two things it deliberately leaves behind: the availability that moves
924	    # hourly, and the descriptions that are too bulky to block on.
925	    write_json(master_min_path, minify_master(master, genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix,
926	                                              age_ix, venues))
927	    write_json(availability_path, build_availability(master))
928	    write_json(descriptions_path, build_descriptions(master))
929	
930	    # Per-day August files + index.
931	    days = build_day_files(master, genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix, ts_ix)
932	    for date, items in days.items():
933	        write_json(days_dir / f"{date}.json", items)
934	    write_json(days_dir / "index.json", {
935	        "dates": sorted(days.keys()),
936	        "counts": {d: len(days[d]) for d in sorted(days)},
937	        "shows": len(master),
938	        "venues": len(venues),
939	    })
940	    return len(days)

943	def regen_from_master(args) -> int:
944	    """Rebuild venues.json + the compact shows.min.json from the committed master,
945	    without a raw scrape. Used to (re)generate the planner payload after a manual
946	    master edit, to backfill it the first time, or to fold in a fresh run of
947	    `fetch_prices.py` — the price cache is the one input that changes without a
948	    re-scrape, so this is the command that publishes new prices. The venue map
949	    (with its cached coordinates) is carried over from the existing venues.json
950	    verbatim; only the lookup lists and the derived files are rebuilt from the
951	    master, which is itself rewritten with the prices folded in."""
952	    master_path = Path(args.master)
953	    master = json.loads(master_path.read_text())

968	def run(args) -> int:
969	    raw_dir = Path(args.raw_dir)
970	    events = load_events(raw_dir)
971	    print(f"Loaded {len(events)} raw events from {raw_dir}")
972	
973	    normalized = []
974	    skipped = 0
975	    for e in events:
976	        if not e:
977	            continue
978	        try:
979	            normalized.append(normalize_event(e))
980	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - resilience over one bad record
981	            skipped += 1
982	            print(f"  WARNING: skipped event {e.get('id')}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
983	    if skipped:
984	        print(f"  skipped {skipped} unparseable events")
985	
986	    # Master: merge (upsert by id) or replace.
987	    master_path = Path(args.master)
988	    if args.merge and master_path.exists():
989	        by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in json.loads(master_path.read_text())}
990	        for s in normalized:
991	            by_id[s["id"]] = s
992	        master = list(by_id.values())
993	        print(f"Merged {len(normalized)} into master -> {len(master)} shows")
994	    else:
995	        master = normalized
996	        print(f"Master rebuilt with {len(master)} shows")
997	    master.sort(key=lambda s: (s["title"] or "").lower())
998	    unify_subgenre_casing(master)  # one display casing per subgenre across all shows
999	
1000	    # Global lookup file: the venue map plus the shared rooms/genres lists that
1001	    # the day files index into. Sent to the browser once. Venues are always
1002	    # rebuilt from the full venue list, coordinates cached. Accepts either the
1003	    # bare venue map (old format) or the {venues, ...} container as prior state.
1004	    venues_path = Path(args.venues)
1005	    prior = json.loads(venues_path.read_text()) if venues_path.exists() else {}
1006	    existing_venues = prior.get("venues", prior)
1007	    venues_raw_path = raw_dir / "venues_raw.json"
1008	    venues_raw = json.loads(venues_raw_path.read_text()) if venues_raw_path.exists() else {}
1009	    venues = build_venues(venues_raw, existing_venues, geocode=not args.no_geocode)
1010	    n_days = write_derived_outputs(master, venues, venues_path,
1011	                                   Path(args.days_dir), Path(args.master_min),
1012	                                   Path(args.descriptions), Path(args.prices),
1013	                                   Path(args.availability))
1014	    # After the derived outputs, because that is where prices are folded in and
1015	    # the master is the record of what they were.
1016	    write_json(master_path, master)

1018	    print(f"\nWrote: {master_path} ({len(master)} shows), {args.master_min}, "
1019	          f"{args.availability}, {args.descriptions}, {venues_path} ({len(venues)} venues), "
